## 1. What was read

**704 research articles** from 33 of the 33 journals on the roster.

A further **232** records (25% of the 936 this month's harvest returned) carry no abstract and are not research: news, correspondence, editor highlights and obituaries. PubMed types them `Journal Article` and nothing else, so the publication-type filter cannot see them — across the whole index they are 22.7% of it and 35% of `general`, and 3,801 of them are JAMA. Every count below is over the full harvest and is inflated by this; the figure above is not.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 480 | 189 | 79 | 169 | 19 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: bioinfo -40%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). Every journal on the roster contributed this month. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nature 137, Science 92, JAMA 75, Blood 54, N Engl J Med 51, J Clin Oncol 42.

## 3. The evidence that moved it






!!! note "Written in arrears, and from titles only"
    2023 was read after 2024, 2025 and 2026, and against titles and journal
    names alone — the 2023 harvest carries no abstracts. Every card is one a
    title will carry unaided; anything a title merely implies was left uncarded.

**A language model trained on sequence alone predicts atomic-level structure.**
[36927031](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36927031/) (*Science*) reports evolutionary-scale structure prediction from
a protein language model, without alignments or templates; [36996195](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36996195/), in the
same journal this month, predicts enzyme function by contrastive learning.
`foundation-models` claims that scale yields capability that transfers across
tasks, and this is that claim as a result rather than as a resource. It is also
qualified inside the same month, below.

**Engineered cell therapy gets a controlled comparison off CD19.** [36762851](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36762851/)
(*NEJM*) tests a BCMA CAR against standard regimens in relapsed and refractory
myeloma — randomised rather than single-arm, which no previous card on this
thread has been. [36356599](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36356599/) (*Nature*) makes the personalised arm
manufacturable by replacing the endogenous receptor non-virally. The thread turns
`forming` on two different kinds of generalisation landing together: a controlled
readout in a new indication, and a production route for a per-patient product.

**The microbiome becomes a dosing variable.** [36813961](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36813961/) (*Nature*): a named
bacterial metabolite, 3-IAA, determines whether chemotherapy works in pancreatic
cancer. [36867675](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36867675/) (*Sci Immunol*): checkpoint blockade itself induces gut
microbiota translocation that augments antitumour immunity outside the gut. One
puts a microbial molecule on the causal path of a cytotoxic regimen; the other
makes the microbiome a consequence of immunotherapy as well as an input to it.

**Resistance sited outside the tumour, measured in patients.** [36931243](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36931243/)
(*Cell*) shows the CD8 response to checkpoint therapy organised in the regional
lymph node and disrupted where that node is metastatic. `immunotherapy-resistance`
claims resistance is being explained by mechanisms outside the tumour cell; this
locates one in a different organ compartment, in human tissue rather than in mouse
models.

**Cell-free DNA carries phenotype, not only presence.** [36399432](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36399432/)
(*Cancer Discov*) reads nucleosome positioning in plasma to recover the
transcriptional programme of advanced prostate cancer; [36399356](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36399356/), in the same
issue, uses fragmentomes to detect liver cancer. Lineage information in plasma is
what a treatment choice actually turns on, and it is a different use of the
specimen than counting mutant molecules.

**What is thin: agents.** Across the 2,968 titles read this quarter there is no
LLM agent doing work in a tracked journal. What exists is a model under
assessment — [36988602](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36988602/) (*NEJM*) on the benefits, limits and risks of GPT-4
as a chatbot for medicine, and [36735264](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36735264/) (*JAMA*) grading a chat model's
cardiovascular prevention advice against guidelines. `agentic-ai` claims agents
become working research infrastructure rather than demonstrations; a chatbot being
appraised in a clinical journal is the vocabulary arriving, and the single neutral
card is all this quarter will support.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

**Neutrophils invert a second time, and now the therapy depends on them.**
[37001503](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37001503/) (*Cell*) shows T-cell immunotherapies engaging neutrophils to
eliminate the antigen-escape variants T cells cannot see, with [37001504](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37001504/)
alongside it. In the same month [36921034](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36921034/) (*Sci Transl Med*) proposes
neutralising a neutrophil product — NET-associated ARG1 — to enhance
immunotherapy. Two months running, one cell type carries opposite therapeutic
prescriptions in the same literature, after February's pair ([36706760](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36706760/),
[36800412](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36800412/)) said the same thing. The recurrence is the finding: what is
unstable is not the target but the premise that a population has one sign.

`suppressive-population-inversion` closes the quarter at 0/−6, and section 2 calls
that `crisis`. It is not one, and the status rule cannot see why. The rule fires
on the ratio of cards, and this thread's supporting side is uncarded by
construction: `threads.yml` records it as a genre rather than a set of citable
findings — the templated block that nominates a suppressive population, deletes
it, and reverses immune suppression in mice — running at roughly a dozen to
thirty papers a month across the eight oncology journals. Six cards means six
documented inversions against that stream, not six failures out of six attempts.
Two of the six (CD200 in January, CD47 below) are the sharper case, where the
therapy itself requires the molecule the field proposes to block.

[36918226](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36918226/) (*JITC*): CAR T cells require their own CD47 to survive in vivo.
Systemic blockade of the canonical don't-eat-me signal would act on the
transferred product as well as on the tumour, which is a constraint on combining
two of the most-pursued modalities in the field.

[36343306](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36343306/) (*JCO*): the high-risk secondary events seen at myeloma relapse
are present at diagnosis, in subclones too small to detect. This lands on two
threads at once. `interception` needs the state worth acting on to be measurable,
and here it is explicitly not; `ctdna-mrd` inherits the same limit, because
residual-disease assays are bounded by the same detection floor. Read with
February's four prognostic MRD reports, the quarter's picture of this thread is a
technology that describes risk well and has not yet been shown to change a
decision.

[36894710](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36894710/) (*Nat Genet*): immune selection determines tumour antigenicity
and influences checkpoint response — the explanation of resistance kept inside the
cancer genome, which is what `immunotherapy-resistance` claims the field is
leaving.

[36521103](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36521103/) (*JCO*): a survivin-directed peptide vaccine carries the phase
IIa readout in glioblastoma, with the journal's own commentary [36623232](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36623232/)
("Antigens Matter") beside it and [36948505](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36948505/) (*JITC*) reporting a vaccine-based
regimen in prostate cancer. Together with [36070539](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36070539/) in January, every cancer
vaccine that reached a clinical readout this quarter targeted shared antigens.
`neoantigen-vaccines` claims the private mutation space is large and predictable
enough to support personalised vaccines at scale; whatever the preclinical
antigen-discovery literature says — and [36890230](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36890230/) (*Nature*) resolves
neoantigen-specific CD8 responses in treated patients this month — the clinical
pipeline in this quarter is not built on it.

[36973806](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36973806/) (*Genome Biol*) qualifies the month's foundation-model result
directly: sequence-based expression models capture promoter-proximal determinants
and mostly ignore distal enhancers. What reads as learned regulatory grammar is
local, and the part of the genome carrying most trait variation is the part the
models do not see. [36890378](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36890378/) (*Nature*) asks the same question of scale in
general.

### (b) Method credibility

Thin this month, and the one card is load-bearing. [36991470](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36991470/)
(*Genome Biol*): the simulators used to benchmark single-cell methods do not
reproduce the data they stand in for. A large share of published method
comparisons — the evidence by which tools get chosen — rests on a substrate that
was never checked, which makes this an audit of the audit layer rather than of any
one tool.

Across the quarter the thread takes six cards and every one refutes, which its
construction guarantees. The objects, in order of appearance: a therapeutic
editing reagent that does not transfer across people, the readable surface of the
literature, the regulatory chain that certifies medical devices, a widely used
RNA-targeting effector that kills its host, microbial genotyping that moves with
its reference, and the simulators underneath single-cell benchmarking. Only one of
those is an algorithm and none is a model, which is worth holding against any
reading of this thread as being about AI.
